name: SN 2001go field (Hubble)
blurb: SN 2001go field, the host galaxy of a distant type Ia supernova, seen by Hubble.
label: ref12-hubble
story: Hubble took this picture after the supernova SN 2001go had faded, as a clean reference view of its host galaxy. The exploding star was one of a set of distant type Ia supernovae that astronomers measured to pin down the expansion history of the universe.

claims.text: REF12 in program 9075 is a reference target at 14h02m00.95s, +05d00m59.18s for type Ia supernova work
SN 2001go is a type Ia supernova at 14h02m00.9s, +05d00m59s, with a host close to the supernova position
Most of these supernovae have supernova-free reference images taken with ACS in Cycle 10
These high-redshift type Ia supernovae were measured for cosmology (Union2 compilation)
